design.title: Look at Berlin at the borrowed eyes' native scale: the 128 px frame is resized in-graph to 224 px (ImageNet's training resolution) before the pretrained trunk, so its 8x8/4x4 place maps become 14x14/7x7
design.init_strategy: pretrained:mobilenet_v3_small IMAGENET1K_V1 features[0..10] (torchvision, BSD-3), unchanged from experiments 12-14
design.eli5: We borrowed a pair of eyes trained on a million everyday photos, but we have been showing them Berlin through a keyhole: our camera frames are about half the size of the pictures those eyes learned on, so every roof and street looks shrunken and blurry to them. This experiment simply enlarges each frame to the size the eyes are used to before they look. Nothing new is learned or added — the same eyes just get to see the city at the scale where they are good at telling what is permanent (the street grid, the buildings) from what changes between photo flights (cars, shadows, colours).
design.hypothesis: Builds directly on experiments 12-14, the only designs on this ruler that moved the held-out photograph: swapping in an ImageNet-pretrained trunk took truedop_2024 from 10.75% to 49.5% usable (exp 12), reading it two blocks deeper took it to 60.25% (exp 13), and mixing survey style inside it took it to 65.5% (exp 14, usable 0.655 / false fix 0.05 / abstain 0.295, mission 0.395). Every gain came from the pretrained trunk's invariance doing more of the work. Meanwhile the training photographs sit at 95.5-97% usable at the same held-out viewpoints (train_capture_diagnostics 0.058 / 0.033 / 0.043) and the clean survey diagnostic has stopped moving (xs_cos_same 0.657 -> 0.656, wpv 0.236 -> 0.240, xsurvey_agree 0.74 -> 0.72 from exp 13 to 14): MixStyle helped the score without making the embedding of a place any more survey-independent, so the remaining 30-point gap is the trunk not yet describing a place in survey-free terms. One thing about how the trunk is used has never been questioned: SCALE. MobileNetV3-Small learned its invariant features on 224 px images, but we feed it 128 px, so every filter sees structure at 0.57x the size it was trained on, its stem throws away half the resolution at the first layer (2 m per feature after the stem), and the deep 96-channel level we read is a 4x4 map — 16 samples of 32 m each, averaged into the place feature. Train/test resolution mismatch is a known, large effect on pretrained-feature transfer (Touvron et al., FixRes, NeurIPS 2019), and here it is compounded by the GAP over a tiny map: a single car, shadow or construction patch that differs between surveys owns 1/16 of the deep descriptor. Resizing the frame to 224 px in-graph changes no weights and adds no parameters: the same pretrained filters see roofs, street edges and tree crowns at the scale their invariance was learned at, and the place feature averages 196 (mid) and 49 (deep) cells instead of 64 and 16, diluting survey-specific transients. This is the input-scale/decode-resolution family, absent from all 97 experiments in either database.
